Consult Summary:
- Fever with night sweats and systemic symptoms for 7 days after travel to Vietnam; evaluation for infectious etiology including malaria planned with clinic visit and blood testing.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 7-day history of fever with hot/cold sweats, fatigue, generalized myalgia, nausea, poor appetite; intermittent fever with fluctuating temperature.
- Associated symptoms: minimal nausea; no cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms; headaches present but described as baseline for migraines.
- Medications: OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol (dose/frequency: documented as recommended daily dose; effect only modest). Seroxat (dose/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: pollen allergy (hay fever).
- Past medical history: chronic back pain; under physiotherapist for posture-related back issues.
- Travel history: recent travel to Vietnam (returned ~4 weeks ago); engaged in trekking and rural countryside activities; exposure to rural environments.
- Prophylaxis: malaria prophylaxis taken; exact agents recalled imperfectly (daily regimen; a second agent taken on top of the first).
- Social history: works as a nurse; non-smoker; moderate alcohol use; exercises moderately several times weekly.
- Vaccinations: up to date with Hepatitis B and other recommended vaccines.

Examination:
- Not performed/not documented in transcript.

Impression:
- Fever with systemic symptoms of unclear etiology; recent travel to Vietnam with rural exposure raises concern for malaria or other exotic infections; focal infection not yet identified; awaiting clinical examination and targeted blood testing.

Plan:
- Arrange in-clinic examination (central London) or local A&E if convenient.
- Obtain blood tests after examination: thick and thin blood films for malaria; inflammatory markers; additional tests as indicated by assessment.
- Documentation of reasoning and tests to be provided in notes for reception.
- Advise patient not to return to work until assessment/tTests are completed.
- Scheduling: admin to book appointment; patient to ring the provided number after a few minutes to finalize slot.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (not documented), formal physical examination findings (not documented), exact medication dosages/frequencies for Seroxat and analgesics, specific malaria prophylaxis names/doses.
- Internal conflicts: none evident in transcript (no conflicting statements about symptoms).
- Transcript quality: generally coherent; some redundancy and recall uncertainty around malaria prophylaxis; no major inaudible segments noted.
